boundaries.notes: Two reports are joined: the Bayhaqi narration about Abu Taalib, then Jaabir's longer report about Utba. The Quraysh are unnamed and not tagged.
This is part of a lengthy report on Hudaybiyyah; the text opens with 'Part of the narration states', so it begins mid-report. Marwaan's sahabi status is unsure in the approved list.

Two reports are joined; the second is headed 'Hadhrat Faatima Weeps at the Pale Appearance of Rasulullaah'. A Tabraani footnote on the narrator Abyan bin Sufyaan is not tagged. Faatima is the Prophet's daughter.

Three reports are joined, followed by a footnote that Ahmad's narrators are authentic. Anas is tagged subject because he is sent on the errand and asks questions. The person sent by Abu Moosa is unnamed.

Aa'isha's report, Ibn Is'haaq's report, a Bukhari Hadith and the editor's note on Ibn Is'haaq are combined. Bukhari is a collector and is not tagged. The Companions named are tagged subject because they accept Islaam in the narration.
Three strands are joined: Ibn Is'haaq's account, Habba Urani's report, and Ali's own remark about Abu Taalib at Nakhla. Habba Urani's sahabi status is not stated.
The text says a considerable portion of this Hadith is still to be mentioned, and that part is not in this chunk. Abu Umaama is tagged subject because he asks the question that starts the report.

Two reports are joined: Amr's own hadith and the Khaalid account introduced by 'according to another narration'. The text calls Sa'eed bin Al Aas 'Abu Uhayha' (his kunya), and that is tagged as the approved entry. OCR damage at 'constantly remained' and 'accompanied (RA)'.
Several reports are joined, with 'according to another narration' markers. The camel incident is from Abdullaah bin Abdir Rahmaan Adawi. OCR damage affects part of the Dimaad report.
Two narrations are joined ('according to another narration' gives the reason he refused). The text ends with an OCR mark '(i)'.

Two reports are joined. The Baladawiyyah man and his grandfather are unnamed and are not tagged. The sentence 'stroked the head of this Sahabi' sits next to Anas's name and is ambiguous, so it is not tagged.
Contains a second report (Bayhaqi / Ibn Abi Shayba variant with an alternate verse). OCR has run a Qur'aan reference into the middle of the story.

OCR gap mid-narration ('so that he However, my people are opposing me'). The text ends mid-sentence at 'Hadhrat Abu Bakr'. Vocab lists the narrator as sahabi no although the text gives (RA); the approved id was used.
Includes a separate Zuhri report about the Kindah tribe. The OCR garbles the Bujra passage ('a man of their tribe who could not perform-the Hajj'); the 'old man' is taken to be Bujra from context.
Includes a separate Kalbi report about Abu Lahab's remarks. The Kindah, Banu Bakr and Banu Aamir are tribes and were not tagged as people.
The second report (Hassaan on Umar and Zinneeraa) is OCR-garbled and ends abruptly after 'started torturing her as well'. The slave girl of Banu Amr bin Mu'ammil is unnamed.

Joins Ali's account, a second narration on the Aws and Khazraj pledge, and a report on the Quraqir battle. Shaybaan and Persian groups are not tagged as people. Sahabi status of the four Shaybaan leaders is not in the approved list.
Joins Ali's speech on the Ansaar and Umm Sa'd's report on the Aqaba pledges. The two sons of Afraa are unnamed. Abu Sirma is quoted for a couplet.
Three separate reports are joined, including one from a man of Banu Maalik bin Kinnana who is unnamed. OCR errors are present. The text refers back to the Ukaaz account in an earlier chapter.
The two thieves of Aslam, called Muhaanaan and renamed Mukramaan, were not tagged because they appear only by nickname. The text ends with 'The Hadith still continues after this.'
Two reports are joined under one heading. OCR garbles the first sentence ('conveyed the of Islaam').
Two separate narrations are joined. The messenger in the second report is unnamed.
The text ends with 'The Hadith continues after this.' Saba is a figure in a genealogy and was not tagged.

Joins Urwa's two reports. The text gives Urwa (RA), but he is generally regarded as a Tabi'i, so sahabi is marked unsure. Some words are OCR-garbled ('Allaph'). Raafi bin Maalik is not matched to the approved entry 'Raafi'.
A second narration (a shorter version reported by Abu Ya'la and a Bayhaqi citation) is joined to the first. The Surah Maa'idah verse is quoted in the text.
The report continues in a later chapter (on appointing leaders). 'Hadhrat Urridr' is named only once and his identity is unclear.
Cut off mid-sentence at the start of Khaalid's letter.

Two reports joined: Alqama's account, cut off mid-sentence after 'Rasulullaah spi? responded' (OCR garbled), and Miswar's report on sending Companions abroad. Isa is named with RA in the text but tagged as a prophet, not a Companion. Several names are garbled by OCR. Jayfar and Abbaad are the two sons of Julunda.

Several reports joined: Dihya's mission, the court reaction, the high priest's death, Sa'eed bin Abi Raashid's report of the Tanookh envoy, and the Prophet's letter and remarks. The scribe 'Mu'aawiya' is not given a father's name; he is probably Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan but is left unlinked. Ibraheem is named as the Prophet's ancestor in a reference to 'your father Ibraheem'. Some OCR garble.

Abu Sufyaan's account is joined to Ibn Naatoor's report of Heraclius's astrology and gathering of the Romans. The Prophet is called 'Ibn Abi Kabsha' by Abu Sufyaan. Heraclius's friend and the chief of Busra are unnamed.

Three versions joined (Abdur Rahmaan's, Abu Salam's and Ibn Is'haaq's). Baadhaan may be the same person as Baadaam in n00105 and Baadhaan in n00104; not linked. Abdur Rahmaan bin Abd Qaari may be the approved abdur-rahmaan-al-qaari; not linked, to confirm.
Joins the Caesar mission (which refers back to the Heraclius section) with a Bazzaar report of the San'aa envoys. The San'aa governor is unnamed.

Several reports joined (the letter, the mubaahala, the treaty, Abu Alqama's conversion, the monk's visit, and the letter to the priests). The grandfather who narrates the first part is unnamed. Mughiera in the witness list is assumed to be Mughiera bin Shu'ba, who wrote the final letter; not confirmed. Shurahbeel is also called Abu Maryam. Some OCR garble.
Cut off at 'bin Amr arrived'; probably Suhayl bin Amr (next entry). The Kinaana man is unnamed. Some OCR garble around the honorific.
Ends mid-clauses. Ayyoob and Ikrama appear only in the narration chain and are not tagged. Suhayl's Companion status is not stated in the text.
Ends with 'The Hadith still continues further'; the report carries on in the next narration.
Contains the main account of Amr's conversion and a separate, more detailed Bayhaqi report from Waaqidi appended with '(l)'.
Continues Abbaas's account from the end of the previous narration (on the road to Makkah).
Opens with an isnaad-only reference to a report already given (Ibn Asaakir from Waaqidi), then the long account of the battalions passing. Waaqidi himself is cited and left out of people.
Ends mid-speech with Hind's words ('Go home'), and the text carries OCR debris including a Haythami footnote fragment inside the sentence.
Contains two separate reports (Ibn Abi Husayn, then Abu Hurayrah) and a Bayhaqi citation; the scholars cited in the reference line (Bayhaqi, Shafi'ee, Abu Yusuf) are left out of people.
Ends with a Waaqidi report about the Battle of Hunayn appended as a separate account.
Two separate reports of the same meeting: Abdullaah bin Zubayr, then Urwa bin Zubayr quoting Ikrama.
Cut off mid-sentence at 'in Tabaalah (in'.
Contains Mundhir bin Jahm's report and a second report from Huwaytib via Ja'far bin Mahmood bin Muhammad bin Salma.
Contains Abdullaah bin Ikrama's report and a separate report in which Ummu Haani narrates her own account to the Prophet ﷺ.
Ends with a section heading ('The Banu Thaqeef tribe of Taa'if Accept Islaam'); the next narration starts a new account.
Two accounts: an unnamed-source report of the delegation's arrival and negotiations, then Uthmaan bin Abil Aas's report of their conditions.
Two separate reports: Asbaq's account of Umar's dealings with him, then Aslam's account of the water and the old woman.
Continues directly from n00157 (Usayd's report to Sa'd).
Two reports: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith, then Abu Salma bin Abdir Rahmaan, whose report is abbreviated as 'the same as above'.

Short addition to the previous account, attributed to Ibn Jareer citing Urwa. Ibn Jareer is tagged as a narrator because the sentence says he narrated it; if the review treats book citations as reference only, drop him.
Contains two reports: Urwa's on Umar's remark and the Muslims' joy, and Amr bin Umayyah's on Umayr's confrontation with Safwaan.
Contains a second narration of the same event, with an extra prayer for Abu Hurayrah. The mother is unnamed and is not tagged.
Cut off mid-sentence. Ali, Khaalid and Abu Umaama are named only in a cross-reference to earlier narrations. Contains more than one report. Tufayl's parents are not tagged beyond this.
Ends with 'The Hadith proceeds in detail as will be quoted ahead', so the account is cut off before its conclusion.
Ends before the poem that Ka'b recites, which is quoted later. Abdur Rahmaan bin Ka'b is not matched to the approved 'abdullaah-bin-kab-bin-maalik' or 'abdur-rahmaan-al-qaari'.
Contains two reports: Ka'b's recitation, and the letter from Bujayr (quoted as a second report by an unnamed narrator).
Cut off mid-word at 'W' after the date. Banu Buqayla is a tribe and is not tagged.

Contains several reports: the letter to Hurmuz, a second narration with two letters to the Persian leadership, and the envoys. Murra and Hizqeel are the envoys' names as given in the text. Ibn Jareer's citation is not tagged.
Ends at 'The narration continues'. It also contains a second narration with Khaalid's invitation in full and Haani's request for a night to decide.
Ends on Jarja's question. Continues in n00197. The Prophet is referred to only as 'your Nabi'.
Continues the dialogue begun in n00196. The speaker label for the first line is missing from the text.

Continues the dialogue from n00197 with no speaker label on the first line. The Muhaamiya regiment is led by Ikrama bin Abi Jahal and Haarith bin Hishaam. Haarith bin Hishaam is tagged to the approved entry 'haarith-bin-hishaam' if the review confirms it.
Text stops mid-dream, after 'handed them over to Hadhrat Umar'.
Continues the Rustam account begun in the previous narration.
Ends with 'The narration continues in great detail', so the report is cut off.
Contains the family report, the idol-breaking, and a second narration with couplets. The son is not named in this text; he is identified from n00214.

Continues the Ziyaad bin Jaz report from the previous narration. The text reads 'Arrtr' for Amr bin Al Aas (OCR). It is not stated whether this Abu Maryam is the Egyptian chief priest of n00211, so they are not merged.
Combines two reports (Haakim's and Yazeed Tameemi's). The text reads 'Urnar' for Umar (OCR). The Prophet is quoted saying Hasan and Husayn are leaders of the youth of Jannah.

Two reports: Jareer's address (relayed by Ziyaad bin Ilaaqa) and Ziyaad bin Haarith's pledge, plus a cross-reference to the Chapter of Da'wah. Jareer is identified from the heading as Jareer bin Abdillaah.
Ends with a short second report about Abu Bakr.
Combines three reports (Abu Dharr's own account, Abul Muthanna's, and an 'another narration'). The end has OCR debris, which was ignored.
Two reports: Haarith bin Ziyaad's and Abu Usayd Saa'idi's. The text gives Howt's name two ways ('Howt bin Yazeed' or 'Yazeed bin Howt'), so his Companion status is unclear.
Abbaas is recorded as not yet Muslim at the time, which the text itself states.
Ends with 'The Hadith continues further'. Urwa may be Urwa bin Zubayr, who was not a Companion; the text does not say which.
Two versions of Ubaadah's statement are given under one number.
Contains Ibn Jareer's report, a second narration from Jareer, and an account of his trading.
Three separate reports: Salma bint Qais, Uqayla bint Ateeq and Umaymah bint Ruqayqah. OCR debris throughout.
Contains Faatima's account and a separate narration from Aa'isha about Hind. One sentence has OCR debris ('Spies').
Several narrations are joined: an 'another narration' version, Imaam Sha'bi's account, and Ibn Jareer's report from Ibn Abbaas.
Two reports: Muntashir (from his father) and Ibn Afeef. Some words are garbled by OCR.
Three reports: Anas, Umayr bin Atiyya and Abdullaah bin Ukaym.
Aqeel's account and a separate Bayhaqi narration of the same meeting.
Two reports: Haarith bin Haarith and Muneeb Azdi. Zaynab is the Prophet's daughter, named only as in the text, and is not an approved entry.
Two reports: Abdullaah bin Amr's and Asmaa bint Abi Bakr's. Urwa bin Zubayr is marked (RA) in the text but his Companion status is unsure.
The 'another states' variant is a separate report of the same event.
Two reports: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood's and Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi's. The section heading mentions Abul Bakhtari, who does not appear in the text.
The lion episode is given with a second chain (Zuhayr bin Alaa, from Hishaam bin Urwa). Utba bin Abi Lahab is not the approved 'utba-bin-rabeeah'.

Several chains are joined: Aa'isha's report through Urwa, then Ibn Shihaab's account and Urwa bin Zubayr's account of Taa'if. The Taa'if 'Abd Yaleel' is named Ibn Abd Yaleel in one sentence and Abd Yaleel bin Amr in the next; both are tagged as the same chief.
Opens with 'Another narration' and includes an Ibn Is'haaq report and a closing report about a woman of Banu Jamh. The narrator of the closing sentence is not named.
Two reports: Addaas's testimony, then Aa'isha's report of Abu Bakr's words on the journey to Madinah.
Two reports: Anas (the injury and the revealed verse of Aal Imraan 128) and Abu Sa'eed Khudri (Maalik bin Sinaan).
Ibn Is'haaq's account is joined with Asmaa's report, which the text says has already passed. Whether the reply came from Waleed or from Aas is not clear in the text, so both are tagged mentioned.
Two reports from Abdullaah bin Umar. In the first, the father's answer naming the old man is cut off by the second report. The old man is not named in the first report.
Cut off mid-sentence at 'who is known by'. The rest of the account is not in this item.
Ends at the introduction to Ammaar's couplets, which follow in n00302.
Poetry in translation with OCR damage in several lines. The first line continues from n00301. 'Ateeq' is the title given to Abu Bakr, so Abu Bakr is tagged mentioned. Faakih is named only as Faakih.
Two reports: Jaabir's and Uthmaan's.
Two reports: Abdullaah bin Ja'far's, then Kalbi's account of the deaths.

Two reports: Muhammad bin Ammaar's and Ameerul Mu'mineen bin Maymoon's. The name 'Ameerul Mu'mineen bin Maymoon' is as printed and may be an OCR or translation error for another name; check the source.
Several reports are joined: the arrival and Ali's help, the Bukhari version with Abbaas, and the next-day repeat. The narrator of the Bukhari version is not named in this item.
Two accounts of the same event: Abu Dharr's own telling and 'another narration' that quotes him.
Cut off before the account is given. It continues in n00318 and then n00319.
A fragment continuing n00317. 'He' is Sa'eed bin Zaid.
Ends with 'The rest of the narration continues.' The sister and her husband are named only in the heading, so they are not tagged.
Ends at the heading of Ali's couplets, which are not included. Labeed is the poet who later embraced Islaam, so he is tagged as a Companion.
Two reports: Nu'maan bin Basheer, then Umar's statement during his Khilaafah.
Three reports, all from Aa'isha.
Two reports (Hasan, then Anas) and 'another narration'. The text gives only the name Hasan, which may not be the Companion.
Two narrations from Aa'isha.
Two reports: Abu Talha, then Ibn Bujayr with a warning about the Hereafter.
Ends with 'A lengthy Hadith follows'; the rest is not included. Abul Haytham may be the approved 'abul-haysim' (listed as Anas bin Raafi, unsure), but the names differ, so he is not matched.

Three reports: Faatima's account, Ataa's report of Ali's dinar, and Muhammad bin Ka'b's report of Ali's zakaah. Hasan and Husayn are the Prophet's grandsons; the text names them only as Hasan and Husayn.
Cut off mid-sentence after 'because it was not at all'; the rest is missing.

Two reports: the main account, then 'another narration' of his arrival in Madinah in groups of ten with the Ansaar. The text spells him Miqdaad bin Aswad; the list has Miqdaad bin Amr, who is the same man.

Three reports in one item: Abu Hurayra's statement, then 'Another narration', then 'Yet another narration' via Saleem bin Hayaan, who quotes his father (unnamed, not tagged). The wife is called Bujra in one report and the daughter of Ghazwaan in another.
Two reports joined: Abu Hurayra's (with a sub-report 'Another narration') and Ibn Mas'ood's account of the Prophet's words.

Abu Hurayra's report is cut off by footnote and cross-reference text ('Bazzaar as quoted...'). A remark on eight hundred men at the trench comes next, then Aamir's report. Only the first name Aamir is given, so he is not matched to Aamir bin Fuhayra in n00398.
Ends at 'The Hadith continues.' The reference line listing Maalik, Bukhari, Muslim and Tabraani on the numbers is not tagged.
A second report ('Another narration') adds that the meal had no fat or stickiness and that the Sahabah were glad on Fridays. The woman is unnamed.
Cut off mid-sentence ('whether I had become'). OCR has merged the next chapter heading into the end of the text.
A second report ('Another narration') says he asked his slave for water, which the slave gave.
The narrator's name is missing from the opening and comes only from the heading. The Ansaari volunteer is unnamed.
Three versions joined: the first from Abu Burda quoting his father, then 'Another from Abu Burda', then 'Yet another narration' adding the diet. Only the first is clearly from Abu Burda.
Two reports: Waathila's, then Aa'isha's account of the visitor and the shirt, a separate incident. The visitor and the slave-woman are unnamed.
Two reports: the first repeats n00389 in summary, the second ('This narration however') adds the shawl and wake-up details. The man who spoke is unnamed.
Ends mid-sentence. The text calls him Hadhrat Urwa (RA), but the name matches Urwa bin Zubayr, who is usually counted a Successor, so sahabi is marked unsure.
Two reports: Aa'isha's, then a 'reliable narration' from Aa'isha about buying the camel. The guide may be the Ibnul Ayqadh of n00398.
Begins after the three nights in the cave; Suraaqa's story continues in later narrations.
Abrupt and OCR-garbled; the saddle purchase and the message to the Banu Najjaar are not completed in this passage.
Ends mid-sentence ("I met Rasulullaah in"). The verse text is OCR-garbled in places.
Introductory passage that says the detailed account follows in later narrations.
Combines several reports: the audience with Najaashi, Zubayr's battle report, and the list of the Muslims sent to Najaashi. The text is OCR-garbled at one name, which is left untagged.
Contains three reports: Abu Moosa's migration, the exchange between Asmaa and Umar, and the Prophet's praise of the Ash'ariyyeen.
Prose is cut off after Abu Sufyaan became angry. The poem's speaker is not named; it is assumed to be Abd bin Jahash. The book corrects the heading's Abdullaah to Abd.
Cut off in the middle of the final citation (Surah Nisaa, verse 100).
Three separate reports joined: Safwaan's question, Fudayk's question, and Aa'isha's answer via Ataa. Summary covers the first only.
Ends with 'The rest of the Hadith concerns the details of the marriage of Hadhrat Aa'isha', so the narration is cut off there. OCR debris in Abu Bakr's name ignored.

Three parts: Aa'isha's account of Zaynab's journey and care, the Prophet's sending of Zaid, and an exchange between Ali bin Husayn and Urwa about the status of Faatima. Ali bin Husayn is not the approved Ali bin Abi Taalib. Abul Aas is not the approved Aas bin Waa'il.
Ends mid-sentence: 'I was then eight years old while my brother was'.
Author's chapter introduction. The trailing heading fragment is also not narration.
Ends with 'The narration continues further' before the Aqaba pledge. Also contains a cross-reference to another narration. The man from Hamdaan is unnamed.
Ends mid-quotation at 'Surah Ahzaab, verse'. Contains several reports plus the author's commentary. Ibn Hazar is quoted in the commentary, not just the reference line, so he is included as mentioned.
Two reports joined: Abu Hurayrah's and Abdur Rahmaan bin Zaid's. The Ansaar and Muhaajireen are groups, not named individuals.
Two reports joined: Anas's report of the Muhaajireen's words and Jaabir's report on the harvest and Khaybar. The Ansaar and Muhaajireen are groups.
Several narrations and chains are joined (Jaabir, Urwa, Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abbaas, Ibn Is'haaq, Ikrimah). Urwa is not identified and is marked unsure. Abu Naa'ilah's Sahabi status is unsure.

Contains the main account and a second narration ('Another narration states'), plus an Ibn Is'haaq citation. The Ibn Hishaam and Al Bidaaya citations are references, not tagged. Gatekeeper is unnamed.
Two narrations: the main account and an 'Another narration' version. The daughter of Muhayyisa who narrates is unnamed.

Two accounts joined: the taunt with Zuhri's variant, then the Ubaadah and Abdullaah bin Ubay exchange. Abdullaah bin Ubay is the hypocrite and is not the approved Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah. OCR errors in the verse ('Qur'aam') ignored.
Three events joined: the Quraysh letters before Badr, the Banu Nadheer plot and siege, and a brief note on the Banu Qurayzah treaty. Sahabi narrator is unnamed. The Jews are a group.
Two versions joined ('Another narration states'), with differing details on the time allowed.

Several reports joined: Aa'isha's account, the Abu Sa'eed Khudri report, Alqama's question, and Aa'isha's report on the tears. Jibra'eel appears in the account but is an angel, so he is not tagged. Dihya Kalbi's appearance is the angel's disguise.
Ends with 'The rest of the Hadith is lengthy', so the narration is cut off there.
Two Anas reports joined ('Another narration from Anas'). Abu Talha is Abu Talha Ansaari.

OCR-joined: the opening saying is followed by a fragment beginning 'performing salaah' and the report ends mid-quote. The link between the parts is missing from the text. The Sahabi who received the clothing is unnamed.
Three parts joined: the main report, 'Another narration states', and the verse. The Ameerul Mu'mineen is given only as 'Umar or Uthmaan', so he is not tagged. The group of Sahabah is unnamed.
Begins mid-poem and ends mid-sentence ('Allaah shall decide between him and'). The Ameerul Mu'mineen is not named here (see n00487), so he is not tagged.
Two reports joined: a variant du'aa, then Uthmaan's separate hadith on the tribes. Parenthetical glosses inside the hadith are the author's.

Two reports joined (Abu Ayyoob, then Anas), with an OCR cut at 'Surah Anfaal, verse'. The text says 'Miqdaad bin Aswad'; the approved entry is Miqdaad bin Amr, which I believe is the same Companion, but please verify. The Ansaar speaker in the Anas report is unnamed.
Several reports are joined ('Another narration', 'Ibn is'haaq has narrated'). Alqama's Companion status is not clear from the text; marked unsure. The verse is Anfaal 5.
Three sources joined (Anas, Ibn Is'haaq, Ibn Jareer). OCR debris in the Prophet's name ('gjjgji') is read as the Prophet.

Several reports joined (Abdullaah bin Abbaas, then Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Hazam, then Uthmaan's gift). Khaalid bin Waleed is not in the approved list, so he is given as a new person. Abu Aqeel is not Aqeel bin Abi Taalib. Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Hazam is a Tabi'i.

Tabook donations and the Usaama episode are joined, with OCR gaps and a heading run in. The Prophet's name is missing at several points ('was extremely ill', 'was given medicine'); read as the Prophet. Muhammad bin Maslama and Sibaa are named only as alternative deputies. Bint Khaarijah (Abu Bakr's wife) is not in the approved list.
Begins mid-story, continuing the Usaama episode from n00502.
Two reports joined: Aa'isha's, then Abu Hurayrah's. Abu Bakr is 'my father' in Aa'isha's report.
Begins mid-discussion ('Thereafter'). Only one approved theme fits; the rest is battle-strategy counsel with no matching approved id.
Begins mid-exchange ('Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then asked').
Ends at 'The Hadith continues further'. The text marks the narrator (RA), but he is generally counted among the Tabi'een, so please check.
Cut off at 'Then persevere with'. The narrator's Companion status is not stated in the text.

OCR gaps: 'left (with' and 'When returned' are cut. The last line ('Allaah! Also grant Hadhrat Umar...') looks like the tail of a du'aa from another section. The Prophet is not named in the surviving text.
Ends at 'The narration still continues further'. 'Surah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya' is OCR debris, so Mu'aawiya is not tagged. Abu Talha is not in the approved list.

Two reports: Ibn Is'haaq's, then Abu Khaythama's own account. The text gives 'Sa'd bin Khaythama' as the same man as Abu Khaythama. The Prophet's name is missing from the OCR at several points ('said, Shame on you' and 'commended him'). He is tagged as subject from context: the Tabook camp, and Abu Khaythama explaining to him.

Two reports: Ibn Is'haaq's, and the Yunus bin Bukayr narration about Ulba bin Zaid. The Prophet's name is missing from the OCR, so he is tagged only in prophet. The speaker of 'Where is the person who gave Sadaqah' is missing from the OCR, so the Prophet is tagged as subject from context.

Two reports joined. The commander's name in the second report has an OCR gap ('Abdur Rahmaan bin , Khaalid bin Waleed'), so it is not tagged. The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR ('without the knowledge of,'), so mentioned is inferred. Abu Imraan is not linked to approved abu-imraan-jowni (no).
Text is cut off after 'Why did you rather not complete forty'. The guard is unnamed.
Two chains: Ibn Jurayj's (via an unnamed truthful informant) and Abdullaah bin Umar's. The woman and husband are unnamed. Ibn Jurayj has no (RA) marker, so sahabi is unsure.
A second report (Sa'eed bin Jumhaan asking Safeena, a freed slave of the Prophet) is garbled and cut off, so it is not tagged. The Prophet's name is dropped by OCR; read from context.

Three items joined. The Abu Is'haaq citation and the cross-reference to an earlier chapter are not tagged as people. Editorial sentences ('More Ahadeeth ... will be discussed') are ignored. The Prophet is mentioned only as the object of Hind's pledge.
Heading text only; there is no report in this entry.
Two reports joined (Uhud, then Khandaq). The Companions who asked are unnamed.
Bukhari and Muslim are citations and not tagged. Abu Hurayrah is named as narrator of the third item only.
Two reports joined: the du'aa after Uhud, and Ibn Abbaas's statement on learning while on jihaad. Rifaa'ah only relays the du'aa, so tagged narrator.
Second paragraph is a separate report (Ahmad and Tabraani) carrying the same warning. Abdullaah bin Saamit's sahabi status is not stated in the text.
Cut off mid-sentence at '(because of'.
Two reports joined: Abul Bakhtari's account of the Kufa gathering, and Maalik bin Aws's account of Umar's teaching (marked (I) in the text).
The first paragraph continues the report in n00621 (starts mid-story); the second is Mu'aadh Juhani's separate report.
Abu Atiyya's report is cut short ('The Hadith continues further') before Abu Aa'idh's separate narration begins.
Two reports: Abu Rayhaana's (given as a cross-reference to an earlier chapter) and Jaabir's account of the volunteers.
Excerpt from a longer Hadith related on Aa'isha's authority; begins mid-story.
Two reports: Qataadah's (the rest is quoted in a later chapter) and Rifaa'ah's account from Badr, which names Umayyah bin Khalaf as the target.

First paragraph is a cross-reference to a Hadith in an earlier chapter; the second is Abu Saa'ib's separate report. Yahya bin Abdul Hameed is left out (scholar named only in a reference line). Abu Saa'ib is not linked to the approved 'saaib'.
